title: PS5 HDMI Port Repair
subtitle: My very first time using a microscope & a hot air rework station
description: My brother-in-law's PS5 took a tumble when his kids accidentally knocked it over, leaving it dangling by its HDMI port. Time to learn how to microsolder!

PXL_20260824_144640900.mp4: This was four weeks ago, before I even owned a microscope. I had to record the damage using my phone's 5x zoom!
I naively thought I could just resolder the loose pins in place without replacing the whole port. How little I knew back then.
PXL_20260908_080643347.jpg: This is the MUSTOOL G1200D Digital Microscope. I picked it up for an absolute steal (€46.38) on banggood.com
PXL_20260923_165221575.jpg: This was not a steal, this is serious hobby equipment: the Atten ST-862D hot air rework station. I picked it up for €175 from reichelt.com
PXL_20260924_072737842.MP.jpg: I found this monkey wrench to be super helpful for holding the new HDMI port steady while I tinned it.
PXL_20260924_072816706.jpg: You can never have enough flux!
PXL_20260924_073528394.jpg: Cleaned it down afterwards with 99.9% IPA
You can never have enough IPA!
PXL_20260924_074332574.jpg: Time to tear down the PS5... again.
The first time I tore it down four weeks ago, I quickly realised that I needed a microscope and rework station to complete this project.
PXL_20260924_075409989.jpg: I always take a photo of the screws like this so I can put them back exactly where they came from. I have no idea why Sony uses so many different screw lengths!
PXL_20260924_075855854.jpg: More screws, more photos. At least four different lengths and styles are used just for this cover alone!
PXL_20260924_082814676.jpg: I watched at least eight hours of YouTubers doing this exact job. The console technician community seems to agree that it's best to hang the board over the edge of a table and heat the HDMI port from below.
This was the best video I found, Derek make it look easy, it was not: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KBFJtn4Ff3I
PXL_20260924_090648441.jpg: When I finally managed to get the old HDMI port off the PCB, I found a nasty surprise: the leftmost pin (Pin 1: TMDS Data 2+) was completely missing its trace—likely ripped right off when the PS5 was hanging by its cable.
PXL_20260924_082814677.jpg: I had never used a rework station before, so when the fire alarm suddenly went off, I had no idea what was happening. It scared the crap out of me, so I decided to temporarily remove the alarm until I finished the job!
PXL_20260924_090648442.jpg: I installed the new HDMI port before fixing the broken trace.

This was the start of the trace-fixing process. It took me two hours to get it right, microsoldering is definitely a skill that requires a lot of practice! I spent ages checking continuity between things that should have continuity, and double-checking everything else to make sure nothing was shorted.
WhatsApp Image 2026-09-24 at 19.54.35.jp: You wouldn't believe how happy I was when this image appeared on screen.
